qt: to the Commission Alexander Jungbluth (ESN) Subject:

The drag show ‘Mon Amour’ was held in Mainz in 2024 to mark Franco-German Day1. It was developed as part of a programme on the Franco-German drag scene. Students were invited to take part in make-up workshops, queer discussion groups and, lastly, a drag show. This initiative was organised by Erasmus+, among other organisations. 1.
What specific objectives and measurable outcomes did the Commission aim to achieve by funding this show, and to what extent are these in line with the core objectives of EU youth policy?
What was the total amount of EU support for this event, whether direct or indirect?

Which organisations and individuals (please provide names) from which countries of origin took part in the show as participants, trainers or cooperation partners or were involved in shaping its content?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.10.2026) While the question refers to Erasmus+ as one of the organisers of the ‘Mon Amour’ drag show initiative, there is no mention of Erasmus+ in the post referenced in the footnote N 1 to the current question, and we have no data it is funded by Erasmus+. Erasmus+ programme promotes ethics in lifelong learning by encouraging projects and activities and puts a strong focus on raising awareness of and understanding the EU context, notably in regards the common EU values set out in Article 2 of the Treaty of EU and the principles of unity and diversity, as well as their social, cultural and historical heritage. Also, one of the overarching priorities of Erasmus+ is to promote equal opportunities and access, inclusion, diversity and fairness across all its actions, and to involve people with fewer opportunities because of their background, with a view to being as inclusive and diverse as possible.
